prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1001; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left-hand lane and began a left turn at an intersection in Pearland, Texas, when the vehicle was struck on its driver side by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight through the same intersection. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain following the impact and was transported for evaluation. A Passenger was also in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and both the responding officer and the statements taken at the scene confirm that person's presence in the car. No independent witnesses were located at the scene, so the account of the collision rests on the statements of the drivers and the physical evidence. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several details of the sequence, including the point of contact and the final resting positions of both vehicles. The damage to Driver 1's vehicle is largely consistent with the described impact, and the reported injuries appear consistent with the type and force of a side collision of this kind. Nothing at the scene indicated prior damage to the vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
